related_questions.question: What was the problem with the Johnson and Johnson COVID vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) COVID-19 vaccine has been associated with a rare but serious blood clotting disorder called thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS). While the vaccine is no longer widely available, it's important to understand the potential risks, especially for those who received it.

list.title: TTS (Thrombosis with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome):
list.snippet: This is a rare blood clotting disorder that can occur after vaccination with the J&J vaccine.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: The risk of TTS is higher in women aged 30-49, with an estimated risk of 1 in 100,000.

list.title: FDA Action:
list.snippet: The FDA has restricted the use of the J&J vaccine, recommending it only for adults who specifically request it or who cannot have other available vaccines due to medical reasons.

list.title: Availability:
list.snippet: The J&J vaccine is no longer widely available due to the identified risks reported by GoodRx.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: The CDC and FDA track adverse events through VAERS, the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System} to monitor for any potential issues with vaccines.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while the J&J vaccine offered a convenient one-dose option, it's associated with a rare but serious risk of blood clots. Due to this risk, its use has been restricted, and it's not commonly available.
